items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Dan Logan and I were staying together

ctx.x: with Clarence Page. We decided to buy a gallon of moonshine whiskey in Covington, Ky., because it was cheaper than in Lexington someone said. We had some other jobs after Lexington and a gallon of juice would last for a time if we took it easy. We had a few swallows before we left to play the dance. We were all staying in a big rooming house owned by a woman named Kate and all the rooms were on the ground floor. Dan Logan and I were staying together, but Dan didn't drink.

I always had a good time when I went to Lexington and the dance was a jumping one. When it was finished, we had some food in a late morning restaurant and came back to Kate's place and brought out the jug. Dan went to bed and we all gathered in one room and started to drink.

After half an hour, I decided that I would have one more drink and hit the hay. I had the drink and just as I started for the door a voice hollered: 'Don't move anybody!' I looked around and there was a white hand with a gun in it poked through the window. It was summer and the window was open. In stepped a white policeman who told us that we were under arrest. Some more police came in after him and they put us in a black Maria, as patrol wagons were called, and took us to jail.
